summary: 北美大型哺乳动物灭绝的原因仍有争议。模拟显示，即使猎杀量不大，繁殖缓慢的物种也可能消失；另一些研究者则从人类带来的疾病或气候反复波动寻找解释。

paragraphs.brief: 新的发现为这些有争议的假设之一提供了支持：人类捕猎将这些巨大的巨型动物物种灭绝。
sentences: Although it’s hard to imagine in this age of urban sprawl and automobiles, North America once belonged to huge, elephant-like mammoths, camels, bear-sized beavers and other giant beasts, collectively known as ‘megafauna’.
虽然很难想象在这个城市无序扩张和汽车时代北美曾经属于象大象一样的大象、骆驼、熊大小的海狸和其他大野兽，统称为“巨型动物”
Some 11,000 years ago, however, these large-bodied mammals—about 70 species in all—disappeared.
然而，大约11,000年前，这些大型哺乳动物 - - 总共约有70种 - - 消失了。
Their demise coincided roughly with the arrival of humans on the continent and dramatic climate change—factors that have inspired several theories about the die-off.
他们的死亡大致与人类抵达非洲大陆和气候变化的剧烈因素同时发生，这些因素激发了有关死亡的数种理论。
Yet despite decades of scientific investigation, the exact cause remains a mystery.
然而，尽管进行了几十年的科学调查，确切原因仍然是个谜。
Now new findings offer support to one of these controversial hypotheses: that human hunting drove these huge megafauna species to extinction.
新的发现为这些有争议的假设之一提供了支持：人类捕猎将这些巨大的巨型动物物种灭绝。

paragraphs.brief: 这种信念导致了1960年代出现的超额杀人模式，当时亚利桑那大学的Paul S. Martin提出了这种模式。
sentences: This belief resulted in the overkill model which emerged in the 1960s, when it was put forth by Paul S. Martin of the University of Arizona.
这种信念导致了1960年代出现的超额杀人模式，当时亚利桑那大学的Paul S. Martin提出了这种模式。

Since then, critics have charged that no archaeological remains exist to support the idea that the first Americans hunted to the extent necessary to cause these extinctions, but at the annual meeting of the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology in Mexico City in October 1999, specialist John Alroy of the University of California at Santa Barbara argued that, in fact, hunting-driven extinction is not only plausible, it was unavoidable.
自那以后，批评家们指责说，没有任何考古学家能够支持这样的主张，即第一批美国人为了造成这些灭绝而猎杀，而这是必要的，但1999年10月在墨西哥城举行的Vertebrate Paleontology协会年会上，加利福尼亚大学圣巴巴拉的专家John Alroy认为，事实上，狩猎驱赶的灭绝不仅是可行的，而且是不可避免的。
He has determined, using a computer simulation, that even a very modest amount of hunting would have wiped out these animals.
他用电脑模拟确定即使很少的狩猎也会消灭这些动物

paragraphs.brief: 阿尔罗伊假设，最初有 100 人，人口年增长率不超过 2%。他算出，只要每个约 50 人的群体每年猎杀 15 至 20 头大型动物，人类就可能在 1,000 年内消灭这些动物种群。
sentences: Assuming an initial human population of 100 people that grew no more than two per cent annually, Alroy determined that, if each band of, say, 50 people killed 15 to 20 large animals a year, humans could have eliminated the animal populations within 1,000 years.
阿尔罗伊假设，最初有 100 人，人口年增长率不超过 2%。他算出，只要每个约 50 人的群体每年猎杀 15 至 20 头大型动物，人类就可能在 1,000 年内消灭这些动物种群。
Large mammals in particular would have been vulnerable to the pressure because they have longer gestation periods than smaller mammals and their young require extended care.
大型哺乳动物尤其容易受到压力的影响，因为他们的妊娠期比较小的哺乳动物长，而且其幼小的哺乳动物需要长期护理。

paragraphs.brief: 他说：“此外，其中一些物种分布范围很广，覆盖整个大陆，例如Jefferson的地洞，远至育空地区，远至墨西哥的南端，这就使得狩猎的数量足以造成他们的灭绝。”
sentences: However, not everyone agrees with Alroy’s assessment.
但并非每个人都同意Alroy的评估。
For one thing, the results depend on population-size estimates for the extinct animals—estimates that are not necessarily reliable.
一方面，结果取决于对灭绝动物的人口规模的估计——这些估计不一定可靠。

But a more specific criticism comes from mammal expert Ross D. E. MacPhee of the American Museum of Natural History in New York City, who points out that the relevant archaeological record contains barely a dozen examples of stone points embedded in mammoth bones (and none, it should be noted, are known from other megafaunal remains)—hardly what one might expect if hunting drove these animals to extinction.
但来自纽约市美国自然历史博物馆的哺乳动物专家Ross D. E. MacPhee 更具体地提出了批评，他指出，有关考古记录中只有十几个关于嵌在长毛象骨头中的石块点的例子(应该指出，其他巨型动物遗骸中没有任何石块点是已知的)——如果狩猎将这些动物灭绝，人们很难预期到什么。

Furthermore, some of these species had a vast range, covering the whole continent—the Jefferson’s ground sloth, for example, lived as far north as the Yukon and as far south as Mexico—which would have made hunting them in numbers sufficient to cause their extinction rather unlikely, he says.
他说：“此外，其中一些物种分布范围很广，覆盖整个大陆，例如Jefferson的地洞，远至育空地区，远至墨西哥的南端，这就使得狩猎的数量足以造成他们的灭绝。”

paragraphs.brief: MacPhee也认为，人类最有可能带来这些灭绝(以及全世界与人类到达同时发生的其他灭绝)，但并非直接。
sentences: MacPhee agrees that humans most likely brought about these extinctions (as well as others around the world that coincided with human arrival), but not directly.
MacPhee也认为，人类最有可能带来这些灭绝(以及全世界与人类到达同时发生的其他灭绝)，但并非直接。

Rather than through hunting, he suggests that people may have introduced a deadly disease, perhaps through their dogs or accompanying vermin, which then spread wildly among the native species because of their low resistance to the new introductions.
他表示，人们不是通过狩猎，而是通过狗或伴生害虫，引进了致命疾病，然后，由于对新引进的抵抗程度较低，这些疾病在本地物种中疯狂传播。
Repeated outbreaks of a deadly disease could thus quickly drive them to the point of no return.
因此，反复爆发致命的疾病会很快把他们赶到绝无仅有的地步。
So far, MacPhee does not have empirical evidence for this theory, and it will not be easy to come by: such disease would kill far too quickly to leave its signature on the bones themselves.
到目前为止，MacPhee没有这一理论的经验证据，而且很难找到：这种疾病会很快死亡，以致无法在骨头上留下其标志。
But he hopes that analyses of tissue and DNA from the most recent animal remains will eventually reveal the microbes responsible.
但他希望对最近动物遗骸的组织和DNA分析最终会揭示出微生物的危险性

paragraphs.brief: 造成北美灭绝的第三个原因与人类无关
sentences: The third explanation for what brought on this North American extinction does not involve human beings.
造成北美灭绝的第三个原因与人类无关
Instead, its proponents blame the loss on the climate.
相反，其支持者将损失归咎于气候。
The Pleistocene epoch in question witnessed considerable climate instability, explains Russell W. Graham of the Denver Museum of Nature and Science.
丹佛自然和科学博物馆的罗素·W·格雷厄姆：“有关Pleistocene时代的气候相当不稳定。”
As a result, their regular habitats disappeared, and species that had once formed communities split apart.
结果，它们的正常生境消失，曾经形成群落的物种分裂。
For some animals, this brought opportunity.
对于一些动物来说，这带来了机会。
For much of the megafauna, however, the increasingly uniform terrain left them with shrinking geographical ranges—a death sentence for large animals, which need correspondingly large ranges.
然而，对于大多数大型动物来说，日益统一的地形使他们的地理范围缩小——大型动物的死刑判决，因此需要较大的范围。
Although these creatures managed to maintain viable populations through most of the Pleistocene period, the final major climate fluctuation pushed them over the edge, Graham says.
格雷厄姆说，最后一次重大气候波动将他们推向边缘：“虽然这些生物在大部分白日时期都保持了生存能力。”

paragraphs.brief: Alroy仍然坚信人类猎人是巨兽的驱逐者
sentences: For his part, Alroy is still convinced that human hunters were the destroyers of the giant animals.
Alroy仍然坚信人类猎人是巨兽的驱逐者
The overkill model explains everything the disease and climate scenarios explain, he asserts, and in addition makes accurate predictions about which species would eventually become extinct.
他声称，超能力模型解释了疾病和气候情景所解释的一切，此外，他准确预测了哪些物种最终会灭绝。

items.en: Three theories have been put forward to explain the disappearance of the different species of large mammals that inhabited ________ 11,000 years ago.
items.zh: 约 11,000 年前，________曾生活着多种大型哺乳动物。人们提出了三种理论来解释它们为何消失。
items.why: 回到对应内容“虽然很难想象在这个城市无序扩张和汽车时代北美曾经属于象大象一样的大象、骆驼、熊大小的海狸和其他大野兽，统称为“巨型动物””，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The ________, proposed around fifty years ago by Paul S. Martin, blames ____ (Q16) by people for mass extinction.
items.zh: 大约 50 年前，保罗·S. 马丁提出了________，将这场大灭绝归因于人类的________（Q16）。
items.why: 回到对应内容“这种信念导致了1960年代出现的超额杀人模式，当时亚利桑那大学的Paul S. Martin提出了这种模式”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The ____ (Q15), proposed around fifty years ago by Paul S. Martin, blames ________ by people for mass extinction.
items.zh: 大约 50 年前，保罗·S. 马丁提出了________（Q15），将这场大灭绝归因于人类的________。
items.why: 概要已给出“by people”,因此答案只需 hunting (若写 human hunting 会与“by people”重复且超出语义所需，但仍s2词，建议用一词更稳)。

items.en: The second theory suggests that humans introduced a ________ which wiped out the large mammals.
items.zh: 第二种理论认为，人类带来了某种________，导致这些大型哺乳动物灭绝。
items.why: 需与原文原词一致的两词搭配。仅写 disease 信息不全。

items.en: However, so far this theory also lacks any ________.
items.zh: 不过，这一理论至今同样缺乏________。
items.why: 直接照抄原文名词短语。

items.en: The final theory suggests that this period experienced significant ________, which eventually led to the loss of habitat and to the division of the ____ (Q20) that some of the large mammals had organized.
items.zh: 最后一种理论认为，当时出现了显著的________，最终造成栖息地消失，也使一些大型哺乳动物已经形成的________（Q20）分裂。
items.why: 概要后半句“eventually led to the loss of habitat” 与第6段因果一致，故选 cjimate instabjility,而不是同段末的“climate fluctuation”(那是最后一击，不对应“栖息地未失”的长期过程)。

items.en: The final theory suggests that this period experienced significant ____ (Q19), which eventually led to the loss of habitat and to the division of the ________ that some of the large mammals had organized.
items.zh: 最后一种理论认为，当时出现了显著的________（Q19），最终造成栖息地消失，也使一些大型哺乳动物已经形成的________分裂。
items.why: 与“division of the…”精确对应。名词复数形式与原文一致。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词。

items.en: Too little evidence exists to support the hunting theory.
items.zh: 很少有证据支持狩猎理论

items.en: The bigger the animal, the bigger the territory it requires for survival.
items.zh: 动物越大生存所需的领地就越大

items.en: Globally, humans have been indirectly responsible for the elimination of many species.
items.zh: 在全球范围内，人类间接地对消灭许多物种负有责任。

items.en: Population estimates can be used to understand how large mammals became extinct.
items.zh: 人口估计可以用来了解大型哺乳动物是如何灭绝的。

items.en: Scientific examination of fossil remains may provide some proof for one of the theories.
items.zh: 对化石遗骸进行科学检查可能为其中一种理论提供了一些证据。

items.en: Environmental changes negatively affected the social groupings of some large species.
items.zh: 环境变化对某些大型物种的社会组合产生了负面影响。

pairs: 题干用动词，定位句改用同词根的名词。
第 6 段 · 第 4 句
第 5 段 · 第 1 句
points: 回到对应内容“这种信念导致了1960年代出现的超额杀人模式，当时亚利桑那大学的Paul S. Martin提出了这种模式”，再按题干要求写出答案。
题干问“很少有证据支持狩猎理论”。定位句写到“但来自纽约市美国自然历史博物馆的哺乳动物专家Ross D. E. MacPhee 更具体地提出了批评，他指出，有关考古记录中只有十几个关于嵌在长毛象骨头中的石块点的例子(应该指出，其他巨型动物遗骸中没有任何石块点是已知的)——如果狩猎将这些动物灭绝，人…”。
clauses: …, North America once belonged to huge, elephant-like mammoths, camels, bear-sized beavers and other giant beasts, collectively known as ‘megafauna’.
连接词 although 引出“Although it’s hard to imagine in this age of urban sprawl and automobiles”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 although 把这一层关系补进去。
Their demise coincided roughly with the arrival of humans on the continent and dramatic climate change—factors ….
“that have inspired several theories about the die-off”修饰前面的 factors。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 factors，再把修饰信息接回主句。
